Liquid Death spent $4,500 marketing water that didn't exist. It got 3 million views, a $1.6M seed round, and eventually a $1.4 billion valuation. Here's how it did it: 1. It borrowed from the energy drink industry. In 2009, founder Mike Cessario noticed bands at the Vans Warped Tour drinking water from Monster Energy cans. Monster had filled its branded cans with water so musicians wouldn't be seen holding plastic water bottles on stage. Cessario spotted an opportunity. Why should energy drinks get all the cool packaging? @LiquidDeath made water look like a metal band's merchandise. It understood that customers don't just buy products but also the image associated with them. 2. It sold the idea before building the product. Investors weren't interested in funding a company called Liquid Death. So Cessario: - Created a 3D render of the can. - Shot a promotional video for $1,500. - Spent roughly $3,000 on Facebook ads. The product didn't even exist. Three months later, the video had 3 million views, the Facebook page had more followers than Aquafina, and a 7-Eleven franchisee was asking how to stock it. He eventually raised a $1.6M seed round. Instead of trying to convince investors with a pitch deck, he got the market to validate the idea first. 3. It turned hate comments into ads. People called it the dumbest name for water. Others told the company to fire its marketing guy. Liquid Death turned those comments into advertisements. They became its highest-performing ads. Then it turned the comments into actual heavy metal songs on an album called *Greatest Hates*. 4. It engineered moments of attention. Liquid Death doesn't rely on conventional beverage advertising. It creates ridiculous campaigns, celebrity collaborations and stunts designed to get people talking. The goal is to create something people want to share. A campaign people voluntarily share can do more for a brand than another round of product-focused ads. 5. It found the right distribution channel. In a supermarket, Liquid Death competes with every other bottled water brand. At a music festival, its branding fits right in. In 2021, Live Nation invested in the company and made it the exclusive water at many of its venues and festivals. One partnership gave Liquid Death access to an audience that already understood its positioning. Liquid Death generated $45M in revenue in 2021 and $263M in retail sales in 2023. The founder's bet was: You can't own water. But you can own the brand people associate with it. ~ And that's what good positioning and storytelling can do for a business. Drinks Industry Brief | Nov 18 / 酒業快訊 11/18 — ## Drinks Industry Brief | Nov 18 A few updates worth noting for fellow drinks professionals: 1️⃣ Kinmen Kaoliang Liquor's "Yi Gu Zuo Qi" kaoliang, made from 100% Taiwan contract-grown sorghum, has won double gold at international spirits competitions and been certified by Taiwan's Agriculture and Food Agency as a local specialty liquor made with domestic raw materials. 2️⃣ Ireland's Great Northern Distillery has paused distilling and cut jobs; founder John Teeling cited softer spirits demand and monthly gas bills rising from €150,000 to €300,000. The pause is expected to last until the end of the year but could continue until February 2027. 3️⃣ France removed 55,000 hectares of vines across 2025 and 2026, more than 7% of its national vineyard area, mainly because wine consumption has fallen. 4️⃣ Champagne shipments fell 3.4% in October to 29.6 million bottles; shipments in France dropped 7.3% to 11.1 million, while exports slipped 1% to 18.6 million. 5️⃣ Sazerac and Liquid Death founder Mike Cessario have launched Mr. Fancy, a 5.5% ABV canned sparkling wine in Brut and Rosé, with 12-oz 6-packs at a suggested retail price of $15. **My take:** When consumers drink less, every bottle needs a clearer reason to be chosen. Kinmen's answer is a traceable origin story; Mr. Fancy's is a new, lighter format. In sales, I find buyers respond best when we can say in one sentence where the liquor comes from and why it fits their table. Happy to connect and exchange ideas. --- ## 酒業快訊｜11/18 今天整理幾則值得酒類同業留意的消息： 1️⃣ 金門酒廠《一穀作契金門高粱酒》以 100% 臺灣契作高粱釀製，在國際烈酒大賽拿下雙金，並獲農業部農糧署「國產農糧原料地方特色酒品」認證推薦。 2️⃣ 愛爾蘭 Great Northern Distillery 暫停蒸餾並裁員，創辦人 John Teeling 指出烈酒需求轉弱，加上每月天然氣費從 15 萬歐元漲到 30 萬歐元；預計停到年底，也可能延續到 2027 年 2 月。 3️⃣ 法國 2025、2026 兩年共拔除 5.5 萬公頃葡萄園，超過全國葡萄園面積 7%，主因是葡萄酒消費下滑。 4️⃣ 香檳 10 月出貨 2,960 萬瓶，年減 3.4%；法國國內跌 7.3% 至 1,110 萬瓶，出口跌 1% 至 1,860 萬瓶。 5️⃣ Sazerac 與 Liquid Death 創辦人 Mike Cessario 合作推出罐裝氣泡酒 Mr. Fancy，酒精度 5.5%，有 Brut 與 Rosé，12 盎司 6 罐裝建議售價 15 美元。 **我的觀察**：消費者喝得少，每一瓶酒都需要更清楚的「被選擇的理由」。金酒給的是看得見的原料與產地故事，Mr. Fancy 給的是更輕鬆的新包裝。跑業務這些年，我發現能用一句話講清楚「這酒從哪裡來、為什麼適合你的餐桌」，客人最容易點頭。 歡迎同業一起交流。
